page: Amazon Web Services m6gd.medium is a general-purpose, ARM-based virtual machine instance powered by a dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. Operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz, this instance features 1 physical core and 1 vCPU with a single thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It is equipped with 59 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, delivering low-latency local disk access directly attached via the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates that the single-core processing performance of the Graviton processor falls within the average range, as demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 1493.49. However, due to its single-vCPU limitation, multi-core and parallel processing metrics are constrained, resulting in lower relative performance across multi-threaded workloads, including software compilation and image processing. Memory bandwidth tests show 59.37 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 19.34 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Database operations, such as Redis SET, achieve 1.18 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reaches 1.15 GB/sec.

The m6gd.medium offers a cost-efficient entry point for ARM64 architecture development and testing, combining dedicated CPU allocation with high-speed local NVMe storage. The inclusion of local SSD storage eliminates the need for external block storage for temporary data, optimizing resource density for lightweight workloads. This instance is best suited for low-traffic web servers, microservices, local caching, software development, and lightweight database applications that do not require high multi-threaded performance or extensive memory capacity.
